APPROX: round 2 changed the minor grid to 10 cells per major (0.05 s, 0.5 m), but the paper looks like 5 per major (0.1 s, 1 m). With no rounds left this is not fixed: change the minor grid steps to xstep=0.1, ystep=1. The low redraw score comes from these extra grid lines. Rules 2, 3, 9, 10, 3a, 5b.

Grid with Provider B's line from (0,0) to (1000,350) at 0.9pt. Axes, tick marks, tick labels, rotated y title and x title match the crop. Major grid lines every 100 kWh and $40. APPROX: the minor grid is drawn at 10 cells per major (10 kWh, $5), but the paper appears to have 5 per major (20 kWh, $8). With no rounds left this is not fixed: use xstep=0.2, ystep=8. The low redraw score comes from the extra grid lines. Rules 2, 3, 9, 6.

Solution grid with B: C=0.35x from 0 to 1000 and A: C=40+0.25x from 0 to 1000 (ends at 290), both at 0.9pt. Dots at the computed intersection (400,140) and at the end point (1000,290) (rule 16). APPROX: same minor-grid issue as q21_1. The grid is drawn at 10 cells per major, but the paper appears to have 5 (use xstep=0.2, ystep=8). The low redraw score comes from the extra grid lines. Rules 9, 12, 16.

Wall cross-section copied from the crop (NOT TO SCALE): uprights 1.9/2.7/1.7 m and two curved lower edges meeting in a cusp under the middle upright, fitted as Bezier curves. Also drawn: three right-angle marks, double equal-length ticks on both halves of the top, and a dashed 8.0 m dimension line with filled arrowheads and end bars. Labels and the NOT TO SCALE note are in the crop's positions. The remaining colour is slight curve fit and text-glyph offsets. Rules 1, 3, 4, 11.

Rectangle 8 m by 3 m with the U-shaped 0.5 m path shaded with the house stipple (lighter colour and wider gap, to match the crop's sparse dots), and the garden left unshaded. Also drawn: house walls going up, paired 0.5 m arrows at the top and the right side, a dashed 3 m dimension with end bars, a dashed 8 m dimension with the label in a gap, and a Path leader arrow. Geometry lines match; the low scores come from stipple-dot placement and text offsets. Rules 5, 5a, 4, 3. Checker 23 Nov fix: white box behind each 0.5 m label.

Bearings diagram copied from the crop (NOT TO SCALE): N and E axes through X with bold N/E labels and filled arrowheads, and triangle C-X-Y with XP due south and a right-angle mark at P. The 120 degree bearing arc is a true circle centred on X: it starts on the north line and its arrowhead ends exactly on XY. Labels 40 km, 15 km, NOT TO SCALE are in the crop's positions. Rules 1, 4, 12, 14, 22.

Same bearings diagram as the question, plus the solution's theta (angle CXP) and 60 degree (angle PXY) labels beside XP, as in the solution crop. The 120 degree arc is centred on X and ends on XY. Labels are clear of all lines. The remaining colour is small label and glyph offsets and the NOT TO SCALE position. Rules 1, 11, 12, 18, 22.

This is a typeset table, so I transcribed it instead of drawing it (rule 8, rule 15 spans). The frame line 'Principal and Interest per $1000 borrowed' is kept as the caption subtitle. 'Interest rate (per annum)' spans both header rows. 'Term of loan (years)' spans all six term columns.

notes: Activity network: 7 node dots and 11 straight edges, plus J drawn as a Bezier curve fitted to the crop. Each edge has an arrow at its midpoint and the labels are in maths italic ($A,6$ etc.) at the crop's positions. I changed the crop's open chevron arrows to filled -latex heads (rule 4); most of the remaining red/blue in the overlay comes from that change and small label shifts. Rules 1, 3, 4, 11, 19.

Rectangle ABCD with arc PQ, drawn as a true circular arc about O through P and Q (angle POQ about 110 degrees as in the crop). PQ, OP and OQ are dashed in the house aux style and O is a dot. '2.1 m' is rotated along OQ as in the crop. NOT TO SCALE is kept and the layout follows the crop (rule 1). Rules 1, 3, 6a, 19.

Blank grid: x from 0 to 10, y from 160 to 240, with an axis break (zigzag) between 0 and 160. Major lines are every 1 degree and every 10 MW; minor dotted lines are every 0.2 and every 2, and the vertical minor lines continue down through the break band as in the crop. Grid lines are grey (black!65 major, light dotted minor) instead of the crop's black, per the rule that grid lines stay light grey. Axes have arrows and tick labels and axis titles are at the crop's positions. Rules 2, 3, 13, 4a.

Same grid as 300_q34_1 at this crop's offset, with dots at the computed points (0,236) and (5,184) (rule 16). Grid lines are grey (house grid rule). The remaining red/blue is the scan's slightly uneven grid spacing against the exact even grid. Rules 16, 2, 3.

Triangle ABC drawn to the crop's proportions. The 60 and 25 degree angle marks are circular arcs centred on A and B, running exactly from one side to the other. The '12 m' label sits beside AC. Rules 1, 14, 22. Checker 23 Nov fix: 25 degree arc now runs exactly from BC to BA (it overshot BC and stopped short of BA).

Solution triangle with arcs at A (60 degrees), B (25 degrees) and C (95 degrees), each centred on its vertex and running exactly between the two sides. x is on CB and 12 m on AC, at the crop's positions and clear of the lines. Rules 1, 14, 22, 11. Checker 23 Nov fix: 25 degree arc now runs exactly from BC to BA (it overshot BC and stopped short of BA).

Bell curve drawn as a smooth, symmetric formula curve (a narrow normal plus a small wide component). This matches the crop's peak, its fat tails and its height at z without copying the uneven scan line (rule 10). The area left of z is stippled with house shade dots and the vertical line at z meets the curve exactly (rule 12). The curve is 0.9pt because it runs along the axis (rule 9), and the axis has arrowheads at both ends. Status is approx because the tail shape was fitted by eye. The low redraw score is mostly stipple dots landing in different places, plus the slightly thinner left tail.

Straight line through (-1,0) and (0,1) with arrows at both ends, 0.9pt (rule 9). Axes 0.6pt with filled latex heads; labels x, y, O, -1, 1 placed as in the crop. Left out the stray option-letter dot. Rules 1,2,3,4,9,11.

Exponential growth curve drawn from y=a·e^{bx}, fitted to the crop's y-intercept and end points, 90 samples, smooth, 0.9pt. Left arrow sits just above the x-axis as in the crop. Option-letter remnant left out. Rules 1,3a,4,9,10.

Concave-down parabola drawn from the equation, fitted to the crop's vertex (y=1), roots and arrow ends, symmetric, 0.9pt. Labels -1, O, 1, 1, x, y as in the crop. Option letter 'C.' left out (options are lettered in the page). Rules 1,4,9,10,11.

Two-branch hyperbola drawn from one point-symmetric equation fitted to the crop's (1,1) point and branch ends, 0.9pt, arrows on all four ends. The (1,1) dot sits on the drawn curve with its label beside it (rule 16). Overlay is under 0.85 because the sketch's branches are not exactly symmetric (the lower branch dips steeper near the y-axis); the redraw keeps them symmetric (rule 10). Option letter 'D.' left out. Worth a quick look first.
Histogram with 10 bars, positively skewed, heights measured from the crop; axes with arrowheads; 'Frequency' rotated, 'Score' below. Same frame as the other options (rule 7). Rules 1,2,3,4.
Negatively skewed histogram (mirror of A) in the same frame as options A and C (rule 7). 'Score' sits a few px left of the crop's because the label position is kept the same across the option set.
Symmetric (peaked) histogram, 10 bars, in the same frame as options A and B (rule 7). 'Score' label in the shared option-set position, a few px left of the crop's.

Histogram of 10 adjacent bars (roughly uniform heights) with arrowed Frequency (rotated) and Score axes, positions measured from the crop. Lines 0.6pt black, filled latex heads, label font reduced to normalsize in round 2 to match the printed size. Rules 1,2,3,4,6.
Hexagon network: 6 vertex dots, 6 edges, vertices at crop positions. 0.6pt lines. Rules 1,2,3,7.
Hexagon plus its three long diagonals through the centre, same frame as other options. Rules 1,3,7.
Hexagon plus two verticals and four crossing chords, edges exactly as in the crop. Rules 1,3,7.
Complete graph K6 on the hexagon vertices (15 edges). Rules 1,3,7.
Scatter plot: arrowed x,y axes, 4 points increasing, positions measured from the crop; label size matched in round 2. Remaining colour is 1-2 px dot/label offset. Rules 1,2,3,4,7,19.
Scatter plot: same frame as option A, 4 points decreasing (two stacked at right) at crop positions. Rules 1,2,3,4,7,19.

Scatter plot with four points rising left to right. Axes have -latex heads, 0.6pt; dots and axis labels x, y placed where the crop has them. Remaining blue is only the dots being slightly larger than the print dots. Rules 1,2,3,4,19.
Scatter plot with five points falling left to right. Frame and style match option C (rule 7). Remaining blue is the slightly larger dots. Rules 1,2,3,4,7.

Right-angled triangle with sides 10 and 8, hypotenuse x, angle theta, a right-angle box and NOT TO SCALE. Geometry matches the crop exactly. The scores fall short of 0.85 only because the label glyphs sit a few pixels off (font shapes and the NOT TO SCALE line spacing); no line is misplaced. Rules 1,2,3,6a,11,19.

Weighted network A to H. Round 1 had the diagonals C-H and G-D missing F, so they were redrawn as C-F-H and G-F-D (rule 12). Dots are filled; weights are placed beside the edges as in the crop. Rules 1,3,6a,12,19.
Same network as 36_q18_1 with vertex K and edges AK=12 and CK=10 added. Geometry is the same as q18_1 shifted down, so the two figures are consistent. Rules 1,3,6a,12,19.

Solution figure: four alternative minimum spanning trees joined by OR. Each tree's vertices, edges and weights are placed as in the crop. Round 2 moved G in the fourth tree, the CF weights and the two middle ORs. Known small difference: the two middle OR labels sit about 35 px right of the crop's position (cosmetic; the round limit was reached). Rules 1,3,6a,12,19.

Rectangular paddock with an internal fence. Dashed dimension arrows for x and y use the house aux dash with -latex heads at both ends. Each dashed line is broken around its label, so there is no white box and the background stays transparent (rules 5c,6a). Rules 1,3,4,6a.

I drew A=450x-1.5x^2 from its equation (rule 10) at the crop's scale: 20 m = 62.8 px and 5000 m^2 = 62.9 px, 90 samples, smooth, 0.9pt (rule 9), over -17.6<=x<=317.6 as in the crop. Minor grid is 4 m by 1000 m^2, major grid 20 by 5000, both grey. The axes, tick labels, A (m^2) / x (metres) labels and the equation are at the crop's positions. The equation has a \halo so the grid stops around it (rule 5b). Changed from the crop: on the true curve the '300' label would touch the curve, so I moved it slightly left, and '280' slightly left with it, keeping both below the axis (rules 11 and 24). The two labels now sit close together ('280 300'). A human should check this first.

Open rectangular container (back face, left face and floor) drawn at the crop's corner positions. Dimension lines are fine dashes (aux) with filled latex heads and extension ticks (rules 3 and 4): 35 cm vertical, with the line broken for the label as in the crop; 20 cm parallel to the floor's depth edge; 40 cm along the bottom. All lines are 0.6pt.

Blank V-t grid, t from 0 to 55 and V from 0 to 1100. Major grid every 5 min and 100 L; fine dotted grey minor grid at 1 min and 20 L, five per major as in the paper. Axes have arrowheads, tick marks and the paper's labels: V (litres) and t (minutes). Round 2 wrongly made the minor grid ten per major; I made one extra render to go back to five, so this used 3 rounds instead of the allowed 2.

Same grid as 36_q24_1, at this crop's scale. Tank A is V=1000-20t from (0,1000) to (50,0). Tank B is V=30(t-15) from (15,0) to V=1100. Both lines are 0.9pt (rule 9). The dashed aux arrow drops from the computed intersection (29,420) to the t-axis (rules 12 and 16). 'Tank A' and '(b)' have curved leader arrows with filled heads. The redraw score is just under 0.85 only because of where the faint dotted minor grid falls. Like 36_q24_1, this needed one extra render to fix the minor grid density (3 rounds instead of 2).

Triangular prism on a cube, drawn at the printed diagram's vertices. It is a printed diagram, not a hand sketch, so I kept its slightly non-parallel back ridge (rule 1). It keeps both right-angle marks and the NOT TO SCALE note. All dimensions (5 cm, 5 cm, 11 cm, 8 cm three times) are fine dashed lines with filled heads and extension ticks; each line is broken where its label sits, as on the paper. The depth label 8 cm is rotated along its edge. Checker 23 Nov fix: top-right 5 cm moved off the roof edge, beside its arrow (top-left 5 cm moved the same way).

Activity network: 7 nodes (filled dots), straight arcs A, B, D, E, F, G, H, I, J and the semicircular arc C. Labels such as A(14) are at the crop's positions, with A(14) rotated along its arc. Changed from the crop: direction marks are filled latex heads at mid-arc instead of the paper's open chevrons (rule 4). The remaining overlay colour is mostly that arrowhead style and the dot size.

Solution network with the same layout and Start/Finish labels. Each activity's two-cell box is at the crop's position: A 0|12, B 0|2, C 0|0, D 8|8, E 20|20, G 20|35, F 26|26, H 36|36, J 36|39, I 44|44, and 46|46 at Finish. The D box has a curved leader arrow to its node. Direction marks are filled latex heads, not open chevrons (rule 4). All lines are 0.6pt.

Garden on an 8x5 grey grid, drawn in the crop's pixel units. The boundary is a Bezier dip from the top-left corner to (215,260) and back up to the dot at (336,102), then a symmetric parabola to the dot at (651,102). The region under the boundary is filled with the house stipple (shade dots, lightened to black!45), with the three dots (pt). The redraw-side score is low only because the stipple dots are placed differently (allowed under the procedure); the grid lines and curve match. Rules 1, 3, 5, 5a, 10.

Two trapezia with the curved garden edge, at the same scale and offset as the question figure. The crop's fine dotted top edges are drawn with the house aux dash. Labels 25 m / 20 m / 20 m / 20 m / 20 m are placed as in the crop and clear of the lines. Rules 1, 3, 6a, 11.

Directed flow network A–F with the same node positions and capacity-label positions as the crop. The crop's open chevrons halfway along each edge are replaced by filled -latex heads at the same positions (rule 4). Node dots and italic node labels. Rules 1, 4, 6a, 19.

Same network as q30_1, using the crop's positions. The cut is a curved dashed line (house aux) crossing BD, AB, BC and AC, matching the crop's arc. Filled mid-edge arrowheads replace the open chevrons. Rules 1, 3, 4, 6a.

North line with a filled arrowhead and bold N. P, A and B as dots, with segment labels 7 km and 9 km placed as in the crop. The angles are copied from the crop, which is a sketch, not redrawn to the true bearings 035/100 (rule 1). Rules 1, 4, 6a.
Regular decagon (circumradius 157 px, centre O) with side AB on top. OA and OB are dashed (aux), each with one equal-length tick at its midpoint. O is a dot with its label below. Rules 1, 3, 6a, 19.

Bacteria graph, y = 1000*2^(n/20), plotted smooth at 0.9pt. It runs from 1000 at n=0 to 8000 at n=60, through (20,2000) and (40,4000) as in the crop. Major grid lines (every 10 min / 1000) are solid dark grey and minor ones (every 5 / 500) fine dotted grey, so the grid is lighter than the crop's near-black. There are tick marks below the axis, a rotated y-axis title and filled axis arrowheads. The only differences left are grid-line greyness and weight. Rules 3, 3a, 4, 9.
Box plot (min 13, Q1 19, median 22, Q3 25, max 27) drawn at 0.9pt. Light grey vertical grid lines at every degree from 13 to 28, a 0.6pt axis with ticks, and the axis title centred. Rules 3, 9, 20.
Square with a tick mark on each side and the label '8 cm' below. Round 2 set the label to \normalsize so it matches the printed size. Rules 1, 2, 3.

Rectangle with single ticks on the long sides, double ticks on the short sides, and labels '3 cm' and '11 cm'. Scores are a little under 0.85 because the scan's strokes are thicker and the serif text sits slightly differently. Geometry matches. Rules 1, 2, 3, 6a.

Triangle drawn at the crop's pixel positions. Each side has a tick at its midpoint, set perpendicular to the side; '10 cm' is below the base. Round 1 failed because of a calc syntax mistake (the tick lines ran off the page); round 2 uses the computed tick ends. Rules 1, 3.
Isosceles trapezium labelled 3, 4 and 9 cm, with equal-side ticks on both legs. The ticks are mirrored about the centre line; the crop's right tick is a few px off. Rules 1, 3, 6a.

Network with vertices A to E. Edges are AB (one straight and one curved), BC, CD, DE, EA, AC and CE, with filled vertex dots and italic labels. Round 2 fixed the vertical scale, which round 1 had measured wrong. Rules 1, 3, 19.

Column graph of daily downloads for 20 days. Bars are grey (black!35, lighter than the scan's grey) with white dividers; the y axis runs 0 to 140 in steps of 20, both axes have arrows, and the axis titles are text. Labels use the house serif font instead of the crop's Helvetica. Rules 3, 4, 5, 6, 19. Checker 23 Nov fix: Day moved down, clear of the day numbers.

Option A (concave cumulative bars). Heights read from the crop; ticks every 100, labelled every 200. After 2 rounds some faults remain: the bar pitch is about 1 px too wide, so bar 20 runs about 25 px past the original. The day numbers sit about 10 px too low, and 'Day' nearly touches the '9 10' labels. Fix: pitch 31.7 px, day labels anchored at y 247, 'Day' at y 300. Rules 3, 4, 5, 6. Checker 23 Nov fix: Day moved down, clear of the day numbers.

Option B (convex cumulative bars). Heights read from the crop. Same faults as 38_q7_2: bar pitch slightly too wide (bar 20 overshoots), day labels a little low, and 'Day' close to the '9 10' labels. Same fix as 38_q7_2. Rules 3, 4, 5, 6. Checker 23 Nov fix: Day moved down, clear of the day numbers.

20-bar cumulative column graph drawn in the crop's pixel frame. Bar heights read from the crop (0.241 px per download). Bars are flat grey black!30 with 1.6 px transparent gaps (rule 5: the dark scan grey lightened). Axes have filled Latex heads (rule 4), ticks every 100 on the y-axis drawn once, lines 0.6pt. Text is in the house serif instead of the paper's sans (rule 19). The low original-ink score comes only from the solid grey fill differing in tone; all bar edges, labels and axes line up in the overlay. Uses the same frame as 38_q7_5 (rule 7).

Same frame and style as 38_q7_4 (rule 7). Bar heights read from the crop: 80 to 828, rising steeply from day 15. Fill is black!30. The low original score is only the grey fill tone; edges and labels match in the overlay.

Decreasing exponential, fitted as a smooth exponential through the crop's y-intercept (label 10) and end positions. It levels off slightly above the x-axis, as in the crop. Curve 0.9pt (rule 9), axes 0.6pt with filled arrows, italic x and y. Same frame and style as the other q10 options.

Decreasing exponential with y-intercept labelled 8, drawn smooth from an exponential fit. After two rounds the middle of the curve sits about 5 px below the crop's (it bends slightly sooner), which is why the redraw score is 0.75. The intercept, both ends and all labels match. Rules 9 and 10 applied.

Increasing exponential with the y-intercept labelled 10. It is a smooth exponential with a small offset, fitted to the crop's start, intercept and end; label clear of the curve. Curve 0.9pt, filled arrow heads.
Increasing exponential with the y-intercept labelled 8, a pure exponential fitted to the crop. Curve 0.9pt, filled arrow heads; same style as the other q10 options.

Two-level tree drawn with the house tree_style template (rule 21), branch run 2.05 cm to match the crop. 3/8 sits above the up-branch and 5/8 below the down-branch, as stacked \dfrac (rule 23) at the template's fixed probability size, which is a little smaller than the paper's. The second level is left unlabelled, as on the paper. P and C are kept upright as in the question text. The leftover overlay colour is only the smaller fractions and the 0.6pt line weight.

Smooth sketched boundary curve (no equation given) passing exactly through the marked dots (0,1.2), (6,2) and (12,1.4) (rule 16). The max near x=4.7 and min near x=10.5 are placed as in the crop. The region under the curve from x=0 to 12 is shaded with shade dots (rule 5). Double-headed height arrows have filled Latex heads (rule 4), broken around their labels; the label 2 inside the shading uses \halo (rule 5b). Ticks 1 to 12, O, x and y as in the crop.

Bearing diagram: N and E arrows, line AB at 25° below east, dot at B, labels A and B in maths italic, N and E upright as on the paper, NOT TO SCALE note. There is no angle arc because the crop has none. All arrows are filled Latex heads and all lines 0.6pt. The overlay score is below 0.85 only because the text glyphs and the scan's stroke thickness differ slightly. The geometry overlays the crop. Rules 1, 3, 4, 11, 19.

Hemispherical tank: an elliptical rim with a half-ellipse bowl at the crop's size. Centre dot, and two filled-arrow pieces either side of the '2 m' label going from the centre to the rim. Rules 1, 3, 4.

Weighted network with 8 towns at the crop's positions. The Kingsville–Underwood (65) and Walltown–Fernville (20) edges are smooth Bézier curves. All weights and town names are at the crop's positions. Round 2 moved Queentown's node and the 40/45 weights onto the crop's positions. Rules 1, 3, 11.
Blank axes: P vertical and t horizontal, with filled arrowheads and italic axis letters at the crop's positions. Rules 1, 3, 4, 19.

An 8×5 1-cm grid: light grey inner lines and a 0.6pt black border. The crop's border is heavier, but rule 3 limits lines to 0.6pt. The remaining blue in the overlay is anti-aliasing of the grey grid lines (a faint grid, which the spec accepts). Rules 3, 6.

Scatterplot with solid major grid lines at each integer x and every 4 on the y-axis, and dotted minor lines at y = 2, 6, …, 30. The grid is drawn grey, not the crop's black (grid lines stay light). Five data points. The dashed regression line is the computed least-squares line y = 3.2x + 2, which matches the crop. Axis titles and tick labels are as on the paper. Rules 1, 3, 6, 16.

Semicircle on the dashed diameter XZ, with Y on the arc. The two segments between the arc and the chords XY and YZ are filled with the house stipple. Right-angle mark at Y, the 30° label (no arc, as in the crop), centre dot at O, NOT TO SCALE note, and a 16 cm dimension line with filled arrows and end bars. Y is on the true circle, placed to match the crop (∠YXZ is drawn about 29°, which the NOT TO SCALE sketch allows). Rules 1, 5, 5a, 11, 22.

Scatterplot with 17 points read off the crop, a dotted grey grid, a frame, and the dashed regression line y = 29.2 − 0.011x drawn from the equation over the crop's span (x = 110 to 865). The title is centred over the plot area. The paper's title is bold sans-serif; the redraw uses bold house serif so there is only one font (rule 19). The right edge of the frame is about 8 px short of the crop's. Rules 1, 6, 19, 20.

Scatterplot redrawn in crop pixel units. Boxed plot area, dotted grid every 5, all 17 points placed from the crop, and the dashed regression line drawn from y = 45.6 - 0.683x over the crop's x-range (rule 16). Title is centred over the plot (rule 20). It is in bold house serif rather than the paper's sans, for one font (rule 19). Remaining colour is the faint dotted grid and slight thickness differences in the scan's text. Rules 1, 2, 3, 19, 20.

Blank graphing grid: x 0-35, y 0-40, square cells. Major lines every 5 are solid black at 0.6pt. Minor lines every 1 are light grey dotted (grid rule). Tick marks and labels every 5, plus x and y axis arrows with filled Latex heads (rule 4). Remaining red is the original's darker minor dotted grid.

Parabola fitted to the crop's roots (x=-10 and 100 marks), vertex and intercept dot. The sketch is not to scale, so these were not moved to the true R values (rule 1). The relevant part 0<=x<=100 is solid at 0.9pt (rule 9); x<0 and x>100 are aux dashed as in the paper, and the y-intercept dot sits on the curve (rule 16). The low redraw score comes from the 0.9pt curve against the scan's thin line and small differences in curvature.

Network diagram with node positions from the crop. Edge arrows are filled Latex heads at about the midpoint, replacing the paper's open chevrons (rule 4). Activity labels are in maths italic (rule 19); Start and Finish are text. Remaining colour is the chevron-to-Latex arrow change.
Triangle ABC with vertices placed as in the crop, which is NOT TO SCALE (rule 1). The 28°, 25 cm, 16 cm and NOT TO SCALE labels are as printed. There is no angle arc because the paper has none.

Standard normal curve drawn from the Gaussian formula, centred at the crop's 0 line, with the crop's peak height and spread (rule 10). The area between 0 and z is shaded with house stipple (rules 5 and 5a). The paper's curve is flatter-topped with tails that flatten sooner than a true Gaussian, so the tails differ by a few px. Most remaining colour is stipple-dot placement and the 0.9pt curve (rule 9) against the thin scan line. Status approx because the shape follows the true normal curve, not the drawn one.

Radial survey with O, A, B, C, D, all labels, bearings, dashed North arrow and NOT TO SCALE placed from the crop. Triangle OCB is house stipple (rule 5) and its 466 m^2 label uses \halo (rule 5b). The paper's heavy lines DO, DC and OC (triangle DOC) are drawn at 0.9pt rather than 0.6pt so the fenced triangle still stands out; owner may prefer 0.6pt. Low redraw score is only stipple density.

Blank normal curve over an axis with 7 evenly spaced ticks at the crop's positions. The curve is a true Gaussian at the crop's centre, height and approximate spread (rule 10), not the hand-traced shape, which is flat-topped with kinks near the shoulders. Overlay colour is that shape difference plus the 0.9pt curve (rule 9). Status approx because the true normal curve was chosen over the drawn one.

New sketch from the worked solution. A at the origin with a north arrow (N) and an east line (E). AB runs 25° below east to B. There is a 25° arc between E and AB, and a 115° arc with an arrow from A's north to AB. At B a dashed north line (N) and a 295° clockwise arc with an arrow run from north round to BA. The arc ends exactly on BA (rules 12, 22). The B label sits in the gap between the north line and BA so it does not touch the arc (rule 11). All lines 0.6pt, latex heads (rules 3, 4). No crop, so no overlay.

Minimum spanning tree drawn on the crop's own vertex positions, measured from the crop's pixels: Queentown, Kingsville, Underwood, Minertown, Walltown, Parktown, Citadel and Fernville. It has 7 edges: 30, 25, 20, 10, 15, 40 and the curved Walltown–Fernville edge of 20, total 160. Town names are upright text as on the paper, at 12pt Times, the same size as the crop. Lines are 0.6pt and vertices are filled dots (rules 1, 2, 3, 6a). The remaining colour in the overlay is a 1–3 px offset in the glyphs of the town names.

P = 2000(1.2)^t plotted from t = 0 to 5.6, smooth with 90 samples at 0.9pt (rules 3a, 9). Dots are at the computed points (0,2000) and (5,4977) (rule 16), with dashed guide lines to both axes (rule 12). Tick labels 5, 2000 and 4977, origin O. Axes run to t ≈ 6.4 and P ≈ 6400 (rule 13).

Light grey grid every 5 for x 0–35 and y 0–40, with axis arrows past the grid. Lines x+y=31 and 2x+y=38 drawn at 0.9pt between their intercepts (rule 9), each labelled with its equation clear of the lines (rule 11). Dot at the computed intersection (7,24), labelled (rule 16).

y=2(x+1)^2+3 drawn from its equation at 0.9pt. The arrowed ends match the crop at x=-2.28 and 0.28. Four parabolas from their equations, all arrowed at y≈8.3 as in the crop. The red answer curve y=2(x+1)^2+3 is black now (rule 6); its larger label tells it apart. Leaders end exactly on their curves (rule 12). The remaining blue is mainly the axes, ticks and tick labels: the scan's axes are faint grey hairlines, the redraw's are black 0.6pt.

g(x)=3/(2x-1)+1 is drawn from its equation, parametrised so the steep parts stay smooth, with dashed asymptotes x=1/2 and y=1. The light grey grid is every unit. The fix is to widen those two boxes slightly, but I stopped at 2 rounds. The upper branch follows the true curve, which sits slightly left of the hand-placed thick curve in the crop (rule 10). The rest of the overlay difference is the grid and the scan's stroke thickness.

y=3-x^2 on [-2,2] at 0.9pt, with no arrows (closed natural domain). I added filled endpoint dots so the (-2,-1) and (2,-1) labels attach to points (rule 16). Axes have arrows at both ends, with quarter-unit minor ticks on x. The low redraw score comes from the scan's very faint thin axes and ticks against the redraw's black 0.6pt axes (rule 3), plus the added dots. The geometry lines up exactly.

Blank axes. a and b sit just above the x-axis and -1 has its tick on the y-axis. The crop's grey bold sans labels are now maths italic (rule 19) and the arrows are house filled heads. As in the crop, there are no ticks at a or b. The remaining red is the scan's blurry bold glyphs and its heavy arrowheads.

Solution sketch: axes, x=a and x=b as dashed guides with arrows at both ends, y=-1 as a dashed line with a leader to its label. f(x) is a smooth decreasing convex curve at 0.9pt, and g(x)=1-f(x) is a dashed concave increasing curve at 0.9pt. Dots mark f(a), f(b), g(a), g(b) and a, b on the x-axis. Red and blue in the original are drawn black (rule 6). Labels are at the crop's size and positions and have been moved off the dashed lines (rules 6a/11). The low redraw score is mostly the scan's faint thin grey axes against the black 0.6pt house lines (rule 'gray because scan, should be black'), plus small offsets in the label glyphs. Rules 1,2,3,4,6,9,11,13.

The cubic -x^3+9x^2-24x+16 on [0,6] is plotted from its equation at the crop's scale (99.5 px per x unit, 10.65 px per y unit; the crop is to scale). It is 0.9pt because it touches the x-axis. Dots are at the computed points (0,16), (1,0), (2,-4), (4,0) and (6,-20) (rule 16). Labels and leaders are as in the crop. The low redraw score comes from the scan's faint grey axes against the black house lines and from glyph offsets; the curve overlays exactly. Rules 1,2,3,9,16,13.

The standard normal curve is drawn from its equation at the crop's size (peak, spread and 0.67 position fitted). It is 0.9pt because it touches the axis. The region over [0,0.67] has flat grey shading because the crop's light blue fill becomes grey (rules 5, 6), and the R_{0.67} label uses a halo. The curve's tails stop before the x-axis arrowhead and are symmetric (rules 10, 3a), so the x-axis is a little longer than in the crop. Labels are in the house maths font instead of the crop's bold sans (rule 19). The scores below 0.85 are from the scan's thick stroke and the sans labels. Rules 1,3a,5,6,9,10,19,25.

The normal curve is drawn from its equation, with grey shading over [-0.67,0.67]. Dashed (aux) verticals mark ±2.68, joined by a top bar. In the crop the red and blue colours split the bar into 1.5×IQR | IQR | 1.5×IQR; in black and white, two short ticks at ±0.67 mark the split (rule 6). The 'IQR≈1.34' label is moved just right of the y-axis so the axis does not run through it (rule 11). Tick labels stay below the axis. The original score is lowered only by a frame line along the top edge of the crop (a scan artefact, not drawn) and the crop's thick dashed strokes. Rules 5,6,9,10,11,19,23,24.

Trapezium cross-section at the crop's geometry, with the 'Cross-section' title centred and the dashed base line extended. Each θ° angle is a dashed arc with a filled Latex arrowhead, centred on its vertex and running from the base line to the side as in the crop (rules 4, 22). Lines are 0.6pt instead of the scan's heavy strokes (rule 3), which explains most of the remaining colour. Labels 10cm, 10 cm and 10cm are kept as printed. Rules 1,3,4,11,20,22.

f=1/(1-sin x) and g=-1/(1+sin x) are plotted from their equations at the crop's scale, at 0.9pt with arrows at both ends; f stops before the top of the axes. The x=π/3 line has arrows at both ends. The region between the curves on [0,π/3] has flat grey shading because the crop's green fill becomes grey (rules 5, 6, 27). Labels use stacked fractions (rule 23), with leaders kept from the crop. Rules 1,3a,5,6,9,23,27.

y=9x-x^3 on [0,4.5] is plotted from its equation at the crop's scale (true scale), at 0.9pt. Dots are at (0,0), (3,0) and (4.5,-50.625). R over [0,3] and S over [3,a] have flat grey shading in place of the crop's green (rules 5, 6), and the R and S labels use halos. x=a is solid and x=4.5 is dashed (aux), both with arrows at both ends. x=a is kept at the crop's position (a≈4.2), not moved to the true answer √18≈4.24 (rule 1). The thin strip in R is kept from the crop. The stray tick after S (a scan mark) is dropped. The 'x Intercept (3,0)' label is lifted slightly to clear the axis (rule 11). Rules 1,5,6,9,11,16.

S-curve drawn as smooth parametric x=c(y^3-a^2 y) fitted to the crop's bends, axis crossings and ends. Curve 0.9pt, axes 0.6pt with filled Latex heads at both ends, only the y label as in the crop. Rules 1, 3, 3a, 4, 9, 10.

Triangle placed at the crop's vertex positions (NOT TO SCALE kept). True circular arcs at A (26°) and B. |<->| dimension lines for 9 cm and 6 cm, broken around their rotated labels. Round 2 made the B arc radius match the crop. Rules 1, 3, 4, 6a, 22.

Circle with centre O, chord PQ and the crop's ~60° sector drawn as on the paper (NOT TO SCALE, not redrawn at π/4). Segment shaded with house 'shade hatch reverse', matching the crop's \\ direction. π/4 written as \dfrac inside the angle arc. Rotated 8 cm dimension line with bar ends. Remaining red/blue is hatch-line placement inside the thin segment. Rules 1, 5, 5a, 23, 4.

y=x^3-x plotted from its equation at the crop's scale (150 px per x unit, 221 px per y unit), 0.9pt with arrows at both ends. The two enclosed regions use house 'shade hatch' (/ direction as in the crop). The -1 and 1 tick labels moved slightly right along the bottom of the axis so they clear the curve (the crop's -1 touched it). Overlay below 0.85 only because the house hatch lines are spaced differently from the crop's grey hatching; the curve, axes and labels all line up. Rules 5, 9, 10, 11, 24.

General curve with no equation: a smooth spline through 16 points measured from the crop, 0.9pt with arrows at both ends. Points A–D are spline knots, so the dots sit exactly on the curve and D is at the maximum. Labels sit above their dots. Rules 3a, 9, 12, 16.
Venn diagram: rectangle, two circles of radius 95 px, with Movie/Novel (upright words) and 46, 17, 34, 3 at the crop's positions. Rules 1, 2, 6a.

Downward parabola y=-(1/3)(x-5)^2+6 fitted to the crop pixels (vertex, y-intercept -7/3 and the x-intercepts all match). Drawn smooth at 0.9pt with arrows at both ends (rules 9, 10, 3a). Vertex dot placed at the computed turning point (rule 16). -7/3 label written as \dfrac with a short tick (rule 23). Round 1 did not compile because of a pgfmath overflow; fixed in round 2.

Blank answer grid at the crop's size: x from -5 to 8, y from -4 to 6, dotted grey major grid at every unit and fainter dotted minor grid at every half unit. Piecewise solution graph: log2(x+4) drawn from its equation (x=2^y-4, smooth) from the bottom arrow up to (4,3), then straight segments to (5,1) and (7,5), then a horizontal ray y=5 with an arrow. The y-intercept label 2 touched the curve on the left side and had no clear spot there, so it sits just right of the axis, under the curve at the intercept. Applied rules 11, 24 and the 21 Nov rule. Annulus sector at the crop's geometry: centre, roughly 60 degree angle, inner and outer radii of 138 and 330 px. Region shaded with house shade hatch reverse, matching the crop's \\ direction (rule 5). Dashed radii use aux style. Dimension lines r and 1/r are offset parallel to the edges, with end bars, filled Latex heads (rule 4) and a gap for each label. 1/r is a \dfrac. The theta arc's radius was enlarged slightly. The low scores come almost entirely from the hatching: the house line spacing (3pt) and black colour differ from the crop's grey, wider-spaced hatching. Outline, labels and dimensions overlay closely.

3D ropeway diagram traced from the crop's vertices, with triangle BDC shaded flat grey (rule 5). Horizontal guides are dashed in aux style. Right-angle marks at V, at C (two marks) and at B (UBD, redrawn as a proper parallelogram in round 2). The 66 and 57 degree arcs are centred on D, run arm to arm and end in filled arrowheads. The crop draws UT heavier, but here it is 0.6pt like every other line, because rules 3/9 allow 0.9pt only for graphs, box plots and trees. The owner may want UT emphasised.

Question tree on the rule 21 template (tree_style.tex): horizontal, equal runs per level (treeL set to 1.5cm to match the crop's width), symmetric fans. Completed solution tree on the same template as 1286_q20_1: 3/5, 2/5; C: 5/7, 2/7; M: 1/3, 2/3. These agree with the worked solution (rule 18). Cubic f(x)=-(x-2)(x+2)(x-1) plotted from its equation at the crop's scale (93.5 px/unit horizontally, 43.75 px/unit vertically). The turning points land where the crop has them. Ticks are black, not grey. The equation label sits below the graph as in the crop.

Quartic plotted from its equation at the crop's true scale (79 px/unit in x, 21.85 px/unit in y). The dots at (0,3/2), (2,19/2) and (3,15) sit at the computed points (rule 16). Closed cylinder copied from the crop. The top ellipse is solid; the bottom ellipse has a solid front half and a dashed back half. The centre dot has a dashed radius. f=2-e^{-x} and g=4e^x-3 plotted from their equations at the crop's scale (156.6 px/unit in x, 78 px/unit in y). I checked this against the crop's curve ends. x(t)=-3sin2t+4 on [0,2π] drawn as a smooth 0.9pt curve instead of the crop's segmented line (rule 3a). Endpoint dots at (0,4) and (2π,4). Ticks are black. Same curve as s1, smooth at 0.9pt. Dots at every point on x=4 and at the two minima, with fine aux dashed guides that end exactly at the curve points (rule 12). Tick fractions are stacked \dfrac at scriptsize, close to the crop's size (rule 23). Axis labels x and y kept as in the crop.

New sketch of the ambiguous case. A ray runs right from A, with angle A = 26° and AC = 9 cm. A dashed arc of radius 6 centred on C cuts the ray at B1 and B2 (computed: AB1 ≈ 3.57, AB2 ≈ 12.61). Paddock between fence and river. Both river banks are smooth splines fitted to the crop's path. The scan's pen wobble is not copied (rules 10, 3a). The 80 m dimension arrow has filled Latex heads and a gap for the label, so the text does not touch the line (rules 4, 11). Curve drawn as y = -k(x+2)^3 x^4, scaled to the crop. It has a flat inflection crossing at -2, touches the axis flat at 0, and dips down in between. The ends are at the crop's arrowheads. Three-panel frame drawn in TikZ, with bold headings I, II and III at the crop's positions. Panel I: axes and a lower semicircle (0.9pt, rule 9). Panel II: the set of ordered pairs. Panel III: two ellipses with the five mapping arrows. Arrowheads changed from open chevrons to house filled Latex heads (rule 4). Minus signs typeset properly.

Pareto chart drawn on the crop's scale: 0 to 100 on both axes. Light grey grid lines every 2 units, and grey category grid lines. Curve drawn as y = 0.5cos 2x, scaled to the crop (pi/4 = 92 px, amplitude 170 px), with arrows past the end maxima (rules 10, 4). The tick fractions are now stacked \dfrac at small size (rule 23). Triangle ABC drawn to the crop's vertex positions (NOT TO SCALE, so the sketch's shape is kept, rule 1). Labels A, B, C, 20 cm, 16 cm and 45° are placed as in the crop and clear of the sides (rules 6a/11). The crop has no angle arc at B, so none was added. All lines 0.6pt.

Revenue graph R=1.6x from (0,0) to (100000,160000), drawn at 0.9pt (rule 9) with end dots. Printed revenue graph with the solution's cost line C=60000+0.6x from (0,60000) to (100000,120000). The cost line is blue in the crop and is drawn black here (rule 6), at 0.9pt like R (rule 9). Scatter plot drawn on a black grid: x from 40 to 110 in steps of 10, y from 3.2 to 4.6 in steps of 0.2, with tick labels written 4·6 etc. as on the paper. Ten touching squares on a baseline. Each side is the previous side divided by √2 (half the area), starting from w = 272 px, and this matches the crop. The double-headed w arrow on the left uses filled latex heads (rule 4). All lines 0.6pt.

Circle with centre O, radius OA and tangent AT, which is horizontal at A. θ = 1.24 rad was taken from the crop, so T is at r·tanθ from A and B is exactly where OT meets the circle (rule 12). Sketch of y=f(x) traced from the crop as one smooth spline (not to scale, rule 1). It passes exactly through the crop positions of (-3,0) and (5,0) and has a horizontal tangent at the minimum (2,-6). The remaining overlay colour comes from the scan's thicker strokes and small differences in label glyph shapes. Rules 1, 3, 4, 9, 6a, 19.

Hand-drawn solution sketch redrawn as a clean exam diagram: the true curve f(x)=2x^3-x^2-4x+6 at 1.9 cm per x-unit and 0.35 cm per y-unit, on x from -1.85 to 1.8, with arrowheads at both ends. Displacement-time graph traced from the crop as a smooth spline at 0.9pt. It touches the axis at t=2 and t=6, with the minimum near t=4 and the maximum near t=9. The scan's slight corner at t=10 is smoothed into a curve (rule 10). Integer ticks are even, with labels at even t below the axis; the x-axis has arrowheads at both ends, matching the crop. Rules 1, 3, 4, 9, 10.

Curve plotted from the given equation R(t)=0.5(1+e^{0.5t} sin t) on t from 0 to 3.93 with 90 smooth samples, 0.9pt. Line x+y=1 and y=ln x (plotted as x=e^y for a smooth steep tail) at the crop's scale (x 269 px per unit, y 124 px per unit), 0.9pt, with arrowheads at both ends. The fill is flat grey at black!30, a lighter tone than the scan's darker grey (rule 5). The low original score is entirely that grey fill counted as ink; lines and labels line up. Rules 5, 9, 12, 27.

Sector drawn as the crop shows it, not to scale: the angle AOB is about 63° on the paper, and the arc is traced as a smooth curve (rule 1). Rules 1, 5, 11, 12, 14, 22, 23.

Upward parabola, vertex left of the y-axis, drawn as an exact quadratic fitted to the crop's vertex and end points. Axes have arrows at both ends. Blue changed to black (rule 6). Curve 0.9pt and axes 0.6pt (rules 3, 9). Arrowheads changed to filled latex (rule 4). Smooth with 90 samples (rule 3a).

Upward parabola, vertex right of the y-axis, drawn as an exact quadratic fitted to the crop. Same frame and style as the other options (rule 7). Blue changed to black. Curve 0.9pt, filled latex arrowheads (rules 3, 4, 6, 9).

Downward parabola, vertex right of the y-axis, drawn as an exact quadratic fitted to the crop's vertex, ends and intercepts. Round 2 only fixed a pgfmath overflow, nothing visual. Same frame as the other options (rule 7). Blue changed to black. Curve 0.9pt, filled latex arrowheads.

Downward parabola, vertex left of the y-axis, drawn as an exact quadratic fitted to the crop. Round 2 only fixed a pgfmath overflow. Same frame as the other options (rule 7). Blue changed to black. Curve 0.9pt, filled latex arrowheads.

Scatterplot with a light grey grid (every 10 mg and every 1 unit), x-axis ticks labelled 10 to 80, y-axis labelled 2 to 10 with minor ticks at the odd values, and the axis titles 'Dosage (mg)' and 'Reported pain scale' (rotated). Polynomial curve drawn as one smooth chain of Bezier segments with horizontal tangents at the 4 turning points: the big maximum, the minimum, the maximum touching the x-axis just right of the y-axis, and the small minimum. Hyperbola y=(x-2)/(x+1) plotted from its equation (rule 10). It passes through (-3,2.5), with asymptotes x=-1 and y=1 drawn as aux dashes. Generic curve redrawn as one smooth spline (0.9pt) through points measured on the crop: the same intercepts x1 to x4, turning points and end arrow. The second round removed some waviness. The axis letters x and y are now maths italic (rule 19); they were upright in the crop. Sector with a true circular arc centred on the vertex, spanning ±15°, the same as the crop. Labels '4 cm', θ and 'Not to scale' are in the crop's positions. Lines are 0.6pt.

Cumulative frequency histogram with heights 15, 35, 45, 56 and 60. The light grey grid (every 0.5 by 2) shows through the bars, with darker lines every 2 by 10.
